headline: UK Regulators Plan to Relax Post-2008 Accountability Rules for City Bosses
summary: The Bank of England and the Financial Conduct Authority proposed watering down post-financial crisis rules holding City executives accountable for wrongdoing, aiming to save financial firms approximately £2 billion over ten years.
why: The Senior Managers and Certification Regime was established after 2008 to enforce individual liability in UK finance. Relaxing compliance hurdles aims to bolster London's post-Brexit financial competitiveness.

impacts.name: Financial Services
impacts.why: Lower regulatory compliance overhead and reduced individual liability burdens cut administrative costs for UK banks.
